Sky Control

Bring every flight home at real airports, laid out from their actual runway positions. Draw a path from each aircraft to any runway end or helipad, and keep them apart.

Draw a path. Press on an aircraft and drag toward either end of a runway. Once you get close, the final approach locks in and lines up with the runway by itself.
Who lands where. Jets and turboprops land on any runway. Helicopters land on the H pad.
Weather and wind. Land into the wind: only the runway ends listed under "Land" accept arrivals. Snow closes runways, so tap a closed runway to send the plows. Land MAYDAY aircraft first.
Keep separation. A flashing red line between two aircraft means they are too close. If they touch, they crash.

Airport layouts, buildings, roads and water: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Runway positions: OurAirports and FAA data.
